advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) because its methods operate on two distinct sets of attributes: `title` and `describe_customer` rely on `_width`, while `order_count` and `mail_summary` rely on `_repository` and `_mailer`. Additionally, `describe_customer` displays feature envy by accessing four attributes of the `Customer` object, suggesting that the formatting logic belongs closer to the data source or a dedicated formatter.

suggestions.title: Extract customer formatting logic
suggestions.sketch: Move the logic in `describe_customer` to a method on the `Customer` class (e.g., `Customer.format_for_report(width)`) or a dedicated `CustomerFormatter`. This removes the dependency on `Customer` internals from `ReportView` and eliminates the feature envy. If moved to `Customer`, `ReportView` no longer references `Customer` directly, potentially lowering DCC if `Customer` was the only other reference, or keeping it same if `Order` is also referenced elsewhere. It also removes the `_width` dependency from the customer-related logic, helping to separate the 'display width' concern from the 'data retrieval' concern.

suggestions.title: Separate reporting concerns
suggestions.sketch: Split `ReportView` into two classes: `ReportHeader` (handling `title` and `_width`) and `OrderSummary` (handling `order_count` and `mail_summary`). This reduces the number of methods per class and ensures each class has a single cohesive responsibility, directly addressing the LCOM4 warning.

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class may increase the number of objects instantiated in the view layer, potentially complicating the composition root. Moving formatting logic to `Customer` couples the domain model to presentation details (width), which may violate layering rules if `Customer` is a pure domain entity. If `Customer` is in a lower layer, it should not know about `_width`.
